FSINCOS and m64/mixed precision retain narrow fidelity helper justification; arithmetic cannot be simplified from directory or counts alone.

semantic_review.semantic_justification: Every body reviewed. Trig wraps unsigned angle to 16 bits, indexes 4096 sixteenth-angle steps into four reflected/negated quadrants; fraction zero avoids interpolation and preserves signed zero. Cos adds a wrapped quarter-turn without signed overflow. Dot adds z+y then x; squared adds x+y then z with cached loads. Signed root performs signaling double-memory compare, reload, negates negative branch and preserves unordered behavior. Cross stores rounded components before squaring retained values; normalize compares equality only and keeps z,y,x zero stores. These meaningful arithmetic contracts must survive. However explicit X87Context sequences and arbitrary a/b/x1 variable names are not a blanket math-directory exemption: cite discriminating judge cases per STYLE7, use ExactFloat/named fidelity helpers where proven, and retain narrow lower-level sequences only with evidence.
